name: AWS AI
certifications: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate (MLA-C01)
AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional (AIP-C01)

beginner.summary: For developers, analysts and cloud engineers who are new to AI on AWS. Covers the AWS AI service map, account and CLI setup, generative AI concepts, Amazon Bedrock models and the Converse API, prompting, streaming and token usage, multimodal inputs, the managed AI services Amazon Rekognition, Textract, Comprehend, Transcribe, Polly and Translate, Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Guardrails, a first tour of Amazon SageMaker AI, Lambda and API Gateway wiring, IAM least privilege, cost and responsible AI habits, and a document Q&A capstone.
prerequisites: Has used a programming language such as Python or JavaScript and can read JSON
Can use a terminal and has seen the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI
Has an AWS account or sandbox with permission to create IAM roles, S3 buckets, Lambda functions and Bedrock requests, plus a billing alert in place
outcomes: Choose the right AWS AI service for text, image, document, speech and prediction tasks
Call foundation models on Amazon Bedrock with the Converse API and control cost with token limits
Build a small retrieval-augmented assistant with Knowledge Bases, Guardrails, Lambda and API Gateway
Apply least-privilege IAM, budgets and responsible AI checks to every AI workload

intermediate.summary: For developers and cloud engineers who can already call Amazon Bedrock and want to build production-grade AI applications on AWS. Covers model and Region selection with inference profiles, tool use, prompt caching and structured output, batch inference and quotas, Knowledge Bases ingestion and vector stores, retrieval tuning and reranking, Bedrock Data Automation, Bedrock Agents, Flows and Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, deeper Guardrails, Bedrock Evaluations, and SageMaker AI training, pipelines, registry and endpoints, ending in an agentic RAG capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the beginner level or can call Bedrock with the Converse API, build a knowledge base and write a Lambda function
Is comfortable with Python, JSON, IAM policies and either AWS SAM, CloudFormation or CDK
Has a sandbox account with budgets in place and quota for at least one ml.g5 or ml.m5 instance type in SageMaker AI
outcomes: Design Bedrock applications with the right model, inference profile, caching and batch strategy
Build and tune RAG pipelines and agents using Knowledge Bases, Agents, Flows and AgentCore
Measure quality and safety with Guardrails and Bedrock Evaluations
Train, register and deploy a model on SageMaker AI with Pipelines and the right endpoint type

advanced.summary: For senior engineers, architects and platform leads who run AI workloads on AWS at organisation scale. Covers multi-account AI platform design, Bedrock model customization, SageMaker HyperPod and large-scale training, inference optimisation, SageMaker Unified Studio governance, data foundations, security and prompt-injection defence, advanced AgentCore, model monitoring and bias analysis, observability and troubleshooting, FinOps, reliability, responsible AI governance, Amazon Quick and Kiro, service selection and migration, CI/CD for AI, Well-Architected reviews and a governed platform capstone.
prerequisites: Has delivered at least one Bedrock or SageMaker AI workload to production or completed the intermediate level
Knows AWS Organizations, IAM, VPC endpoints, KMS and infrastructure as code with CDK, CloudFormation or Terraform
Can read model evaluation reports, CloudWatch metrics and Cost Explorer data to support design decisions
outcomes: Design a multi-account, secure and observable AI platform with governed access to models and agents
Customize, train, optimise and serve models on Bedrock and SageMaker AI with measurable gains
Operate AI systems with monitoring, reliability, FinOps and incident response practices
Apply responsible AI governance, Well-Architected reviews and migration planning to enterprise portfolios
